review_candidates.description: This role resides under MISC Marine (the Integrated Marine Services arm of MISC Group). Key Accountabilities 1. Guarantee Claim Administration & Coordination Coordinate the end-to-end Guarantee Claim (GC) process in accordance with the Shipbuilding Contract (SBC), Ship Management Agreement, Company procedures, and established warranty management practices. Review Guarantee Claim submissions from Ship Managers and Vessel to ensure claims are complete, technically substantiated, and supported with adequate evidence prior/concurrent to submission to Builders. Register, classify, and maintain all Guarantee Claims within the central Guarantee Claim Register and SharePoint repository. Prepare, submit, and monitor Builder correspondence, technical clarifications, claim notifications, and follow-up communications on GC related to design or critical issues. Monitor Builder response times, claim progress, warranty periods, outstanding actions, and claim status, ensuring timely follow-up and escalation where necessary. Support Ship Managers and Vessel Teams in executing Guarantee Claims by providing guidance on procedures, documentation requirements, contractual obligations, and evidence required to maximise successful warranty claims. 2. Warranty Execution & Technical Coordination Coordinate complex, critical, emergency, or design-related Guarantee Claims requiring Technical Services intervention to ensure timely rectification and minimize operational impact. Facilitate technical discussions involving Builders, Makers, Classification Societies, Ship Managers, Vessel Teams, Engineering & Design, and other stakeholders to resolve warranty issues effectively. Coordinate Builder attendance, Maker service engineers, technical inspections, spare part deliveries, onboard attendance, and other warranty-related activities. Monitor implementation of agreed corrective actions and warranty commitments until satisfactory completion. Escalate technical issues, Builder delays, or contractual concerns that may affect warranty rights, vessel operations, or project objectives. 3. Warranty Documentation & Evidence Management Maintain complete, accurate, and auditable documentation for every Guarantee Claim, including (where appropriate) technical reports, photographs, service reports, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), Builder correspondence, Maker reports, invoices, and claim closure records. Verify completeness, consistency, and traceability of supporting documentation before/concurrently with submission to Builders or use during settlement discussions. Maintain detailed claim chronology and technical history to support warranty entitlement, audits, future negotiations, and organizational reference. Ensure all Guarantee Claim documentation is properly maintained within the centralized SharePoint repository and related warranty management systems. 4. Dry Dock Warranty Coordination Identify outstanding Guarantee Claims requiring execution during scheduled dry docking. Coordinate with Ship Managers, Vessel Teams, Builders, Makers, Dry Docking Yards, and Engineering Teams to ensure warranty works are properly incorporated into the dry docking specification and execution schedule. Monitor completion of warranty-related works during dry docking and maintain supporting records required for claim closure. Follow up outstanding warranty items until completion and formal closure with the Builder. 5. Settlement Preparation & Warranty Recovery Support Prepare settlement summaries, claim schedules, supporting documentation, cost recovery matrices, invoices, purchase orders, and technical evidence required for warranty settlement discussions. Coordinate with Ship Managers, Fleet Operations, Finance, and other stakeholders to obtain supporting documentation necessary for settlement. Verify completeness and consistency of supporting documents prior to Manager review. Monitor settlement progress and maintain updated settlement records. Support recovery of warranty-related costs, and other warranty entitlements where applicable. 6. Reporting, Warranty Performance & Risk Monitoring Prepare periodic Guarantee Claim dashboards, management reports, Builder performance reports, claim ageing analyses, and other performance indicators. Monitor outstanding claims, overdue Builder responses, warranty expiry risks, recurring failures, and unresolved technical issues. Highlight emerging warranty risks, delayed rectification, recurring defects, or potential value leakage for management attention. Support audits, management reviews, and governance activities by providing accurate, timely, and reliable warranty information. 7. Technical Analysis, Lessons Learnt & Reliability Improvement Analyse Guarantee Claims, Builder responses, Maker reports, Root Cause Analyses, and technical findings to identify recurring failures, abnormal trends, and opportunities for improvement. Identify issues that may indicate potential design deficiencies, material selection concerns, workmanship quality, installation practices, commissioning issues, equipment reliability, or operational factors, and escalate them to Engineering & Design for technical assessment. Prepare and maintain structured Lessons Learnt arising from Guarantee Claims, including recommendations for design improvements, engineering practices, construction methods, equipment selection, operational procedures, and warranty management. Share recurring technical issues and improvement recommendations with Engineering & Design, Project Teams, Fleet Operations, Ship Managers, and other relevant stakeholders to minimise recurrence in future projects. Maintain records of recurring failures, Builder performance, Maker performance, equipment reliability trends, and warranty statistics to support future project planning and continuous improvement. Support management in communicating warranty limitations, technical findings, and rectification strategies to Ship Managers and Vessel Teams to promote realistic expectations and consistent understanding of warranty obligations. 8 . Governance Support & Continuous Improvement Maintain standard Guarantee Claim templates, reporting formats, correspondence templates, guidance documents, and SharePoint records. Support continual improvement of Guarantee Claim procedures, workflows, reporting tools, dashboards, and digital systems. Ensure compliance with Company procedures, contractual requirements, warranty processes, and documentation standards. Support implementation of departmental warranty management initiatives and perform other duties assigned by the Manager. Job Requirements Education Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Marine Engineering, Naval Architecture, Electrical Engineering, or other relevant engineering disciplines. Experience Ideal: Minimum 3 years' experience in warranty management, shipbuilding, vessel operations, marine engineering, technical support, dry docking, or related maritime project environments. review_candidates.title: Executive Director
review_candidates.description: ABOUT CONGO INITIATIVE Congo Initiative is a global collective inspired by Christ-centered faith and united for the transformation of lives and communities in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Congo Initiative consists of three entities: Congo Initiative – l’Université Chrétienne Bilingue du Congo (CI-UCBC), Congo Initiative USA (CI-USA), and Congo Initiative UK (CI-UK). Our work and programs are run by our leadership at CI-UCBC and based in Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo. CI-USA is a U.S.-based organization that mobilizes resources and support for Congo Initiative–UCBC.  POSITION SUMMARY The Executive Director of Congo Initiative USA (“CI-USA”) serves as the organization’s senior staff leader, responsible for executing the vision and strategy for the U.S.-based work in fundraising, partnership building, and communications. The Executive Director works in close collaboration with the leadership of UCBC and CI-UK to ensure that U.S. fundraising and engagement strategies align with global organizational priorities. This role requires a relational and strategic leader who can grow resources; inspire supporters; create, clarify, and communicate a compelling vision; and cultivate a diverse set of strong cross-cultural partnerships in support of an organization working in a fragile and conflict-affected context. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Strategic Fundraising & Resource Mobilization Develop and lead CI USA’s annual and multi-year fundraising strategy, with responsibility for growing and sustaining revenue. Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors, churches, foundations, and institutional partners while developing a diverse and sustainable donor pipeline. Lead fundraising campaigns and events, and identify new opportunities for resource mobilization. Engage and equip Board members to participate effectively in fundraising and donor cultivation. Ensure fundraising priorities are closely aligned with UCBC’s strategic needs and CI-USA’s long-term growth goals.  2. Strategic Partnerships & Global Alignment Serve as a key ambassador for Congo Initiative, building and sustaining relationships with donors, churches, foundations, institutional partners, and other stakeholders. Serve on the Global Executive Team and work closely with UCBC and CI-UK leadership to align strategy, messaging, and funding priorities. Represent CI-USA at conferences, fundraising events, partner gatherings, General Assembly meetings, and other strategic forums. Lead CI-USA’s communications strategy to strengthen brand clarity, communicate UCBC’s mission and impact effectively to U.S. audiences, and deepen donor engagement. Write, review, and oversee external-facing communications and ensure consistency across fundraising, communications, and advocacy priorities. 3. Board Governance & Operational Excellence Provide strategic leadership for CI-USA, establishing organizational priorities, measurable goals, and a clear path toward long-term, sustainable growth. Partner effectively with the Board of Directors to support strong governance, shared accountability, and strategic decision-making, keeping the Board informed of organizational performance, risks, and opportunities. Prepare CI-USA’s annual budget and oversee expenditures and financial management in partnership with the Board. Ensure compliance with nonprofit standards, sound financial stewardship, and effective systems for tracking organizational progress and performance. Hire and supervise both staff and key contractors and service providers. CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES & VIRTUES Cross-cultural Fluency & Humility: Demonstrates the ability to build trusted relationships across cultures and contexts, approaching partnership with humility, curiosity, and respect. Able to represent the work and leadership of Congolese partners authentically to U.S. audiences. Relational Fundraising Savvy: Builds genuine, long-term relationships with donors and partners and can translate those relationships into sustained financial support for the mission. Collaborative Mindset: Works effectively across organizational and geographic boundaries, balancing the priorities of CI-USA with those of UCBC, CI-UK, and other partners. Strategic Communication: Communicates complex issues and compelling stories clearly and persuasively across donor, church, institutional, and public audiences. Strategic Leadership & Initiative: Sets clear priorities, identifies opportunities, follows through on commitments, and operates effectively with a high degree of independence and accountability. QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS Values Alignment: Strong alignment with Congo Initiative’s mission, vision, and organizational values, with the ability to represent them authentically in relationships with donors, partners, and the broader public. Experience: Minimum 8 years of progressive leadership experience, including significant experience in fundraising, donor engagement, marketing, public relations, or related fields. Christian organizational leadership or international nonprofit experience preferred. Fundraising Track Record: Demonstrated success cultivating major donors, securing major gifts, leading fundraising or capital campaigns, and developing diverse donor pipelines. Leadership & Management: Demonstrated capacity in organizational leadership, including staff supervision, strategic planning, financial management, and budget oversight. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, International Relations, Political Science, Nonprofit Management, a related field or commensurate years of additional relevant experience required. Master’s or equivalent advanced degree preferred. Language Skills: Outstanding written, oral, and public-speaking communication skills. English fluency required; professional proficiency in French and familiarity with Swahili preferred. Travel Availability: Willingness and ability to travel domestically at least quarterly for donor development and periodically internationally, including travel to the Democratic Republic of Congo. Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship and able to travel within the U.S. and internationally as required for the role. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Salary range: $85,000 - $100,000 Location: Remote TO APPLY CI is deeply committed to building a diverse team that reflects the communities we serve. We know that critical skills come from many different backgrounds. If you are driven by our mission but don’t meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply. Please submit the following: Resume/CV Tailored cover letter that: Explains your specific interest in Congo Initiative’s mission and how your experience and skills align with this role. Includes a brief reflection on your personal faith journey and your comfort integrating a Christ-centered worldview into your leadership. At least three professional references. SUBMISSION DETAILS & TIMELINE Submit applications to: executivesearch@congoinitiative.org Subject line: CI U.S. Executive Director Application – [First Name Last Name] Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
